title: Ashish Tani Purti Scored 13 Goals in the Tournament. India's U-18 Hockey Team Won the Asia Cup.
excerpt: A hat-trick in the final against Japan, a comeback from 2-3 down against Pakistan in the semifinal, and a gold medal in Kakamigahara. Hockey India's junior pipeline keeps delivering.
body:
The final at Kakamigahara lasted 60 minutes. It was effectively over in 34.

India's U-18 men's hockey team demolished hosts Japan 4-1 in Saturday's Asia Cup final, with Ashish Tani Purti scoring a hat-trick to cap one of the most dominant junior tournament campaigns in recent memory. Captain Ketan Kushwaha added the fourth. Japan's Numada Gaku scored a late consolation from a penalty stroke, but by then the result had been settled for a full quarter.

Tani Purti's hat-trick in the final brought his tournament tally to 13 goals — comfortably the top scorer of the competition. He was also named Player of the Match. Teammate Ayush Rajak won the Best Goalkeeper award. India didn't just win; they swept the individual honors too.

## A Final That Was Over Before Halftime

India set the tone within 90 seconds, earning a penalty corner that Tani Purti converted in the second minute. Japan pushed back, mounting four dangerous circle penetrations in the first quarter, but India's backline held firm.

The second quarter was ruthless. Japan earned a penalty corner of their own but couldn't equalize. India's response was immediate — a penalty corner in the 28th minute that Tani Purti dispatched with a blistering drag-flick. Two minutes later, Prahalad Rajbhar intercepted in a dangerous area, surged forward, and set up Kushwaha, who finished coolly to make it 3-0 at halftime.

Tani Purti completed his hat-trick in the 34th minute after a silky midfield run by Varinder Singh drew yet another penalty corner. At 4-0, the championship was India's to lose, and they never came close to doing so.

## The Semifinal Was the Real Drama

If the final was clinical, the semifinal against Pakistan was chaos — and ultimately the more memorable match.

India led 1-0 through a Tani Purti penalty stroke in the 12th minute. Pakistan equalized before halftime when Adeel broke through the defense. The third quarter belonged to Pakistan: Shahrukh Ali scored to make it 2-1 for India, Muhammad Farhan Aslam leveled immediately at 2-2, and Uzair Ahmed Qureshi converted a penalty corner to give Pakistan a 3-2 lead heading into the final quarter.

What followed was 15 minutes of relentless Indian pressure. Pakistan's Muzammil Saeed received a green card in the 46th minute, and India pounced. Tani Purti scored from the second penalty corner in the 49th minute to level at 3-3. In the 53rd minute, he completed his hat-trick to make it 4-3. Three minutes later, he scored again — his fourth of the match — to seal a 5-3 comeback victory.

## What It Means

Hockey India announced cash rewards of INR 3 lakh per player for the gold medal squad, with INR 1.5 lakh for each support staff member. The Indian U-18 women's team also earned recognition, taking bronze in their tournament and receiving INR 1 lakh per player. Nausheen Naz was the women's tournament top scorer with 12 goals.

For the Indian hockey ecosystem, results like these are the dividend of sustained investment in the junior pipeline. The senior men's team won Olympic bronze in Tokyo and has been a consistent force in the Pro League. But it's the junior production line — scouting programs in Jharkhand, Odisha, and Punjab, academy structures that identify talent early — that keeps the talent flowing.

Tani Purti, the tournament's most dangerous player, will be a name to watch. Thirteen goals in a continental championship at 17 is the kind of statistic that scouts circle. For the diaspora community that has followed Indian hockey's resurgence since that bronze in Tokyo, the Asia Cup gold is another marker that the pipeline is working — and that the next generation is ready.
